newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana-Pacific to close plywood plants.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana-Pacific to close plywood plants.

text.p: Louisiana-Pacific Corp. said Tuesday it will temporarily close six of its seven plywood plants on Monday.
The closure, which is expected to last two weeks, is necessary because of log shortages caused by unusually rainy weather in east Texas and Louisiana, the company said.
Only the building products company's plant in Jasper, Texas, will remain open.
The plants that will be closed are in Urania and Logansport, La.; and New Waverly, Cleveland, Lufkin and Bon Wier, all in Texas.
"We're hopeful that the weather will cooperate and we will be able to build up our plywood log inventories by mid February," said Rick Frost, vice president of timber and procurement.
Despite the curtailment, Portland, Ore.-based Louisiana-Pacific said it has sufficient inventory to meet the needs of its contract plywood customers with no interruption.
Louisiana-Pacific's stock edged down 12.5 cents to $20.75 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.
